pages.title: Build your next world.
pages.description: Build 2D and 3D games with a Java library that brings rendering, physics, audio, and UI together.

sections.title: A complete toolkit. A world of possibilities.
sections.description: Keep your game in Java. Choose the systems you need, own your application loop, and build from a small scene to a complete game.

sections.title: This website is the demo.
sections.description: The visible interface is drawn by a Java Valthorne application compiled for the browser with TeaVM. A small HTML companion keeps the content accessible and the links usable.

cards.title: Java, all the way to the browser
cards.text: Valthorne owns the application lifecycle and UI drawing. Browser integration supplies scrolling, URLs, accessible links, and native text entry.
cards.label: Try the live canvas

cards.title: Start with one dependency
cards.text:
io.github.tehnewb:Valthorne:2.0.0
Java 25. Native dependencies included.
cards.label: Start building

pages.title: A library for the whole game.
pages.description: An explicit Java application lifecycle, a broad set of game systems, and control over how they fit together.

cards.title: 2D graphics
cards.text: Texture batching, sprites, TrueType fonts, Slug vector fonts, animation, Tiled maps, viewport scaling, and particle emitters.
cards.label: Read the graphics guides

cards.title: 3D rendering
cards.text: Models and materials, scene graphs, billboards, perspective and orthographic cameras, raster lighting, shadow maps, and an optional Filament renderer.
cards.label: Read the 3D guides

cards.title: Lighting and effects
cards.text: Batched 2D lights, raycast shadows, radiance cascades, custom shaders, and optional path tracing. Availability depends on the graphics backend.
cards.label: Explore lighting

cards.title: Physics and motion
cards.text: Jolt 3D physics provides rigid bodies, collision layers, contacts, shapes, distance joints, and raycasts. Particle emitters can interact with physics.
cards.label: Physics documentation

cards.title: Interface and input
cards.text: Yoga layouts, texture and NanoVG controls, virtual lists and tables, shared editing behavior, themes, keyboard and mouse routing.
cards.label: UI documentation

cards.title: Sound and assets
cards.text: WAV, MP3, and Vorbis sound; playback, queues, streaming, and attenuation. Asset loaders support asynchronous preparation and explicit disposal.
cards.label: Audio documentation

cards.title: Application foundations
cards.text: Events, scenes, state machines, scheduling, plugins, diagnostics, collections, pooling, binary buffers, file utilities, compression, and hashing.
cards.label: Browse every system

sections.title: Choose your target
sections.description: The stable desktop library is 2.0.0. The browser target is in active development and does not provide every desktop API or native integration.

cards.title: Windows, Linux, macOS
cards.text: Java 25 with a matching CPU architecture and OpenGL 3.3 core for standard rendering. macOS needs -XstartOnFirstThread; Linux needs a graphical session and the documented native system libraries.
cards.label: Desktop requirements

cards.title: Browser · in development
cards.text: TeaVM compiles Java to JavaScript. Browser backends support UI and graphics, with WebGL 2 and optional WebAssembly libraries for systems such as Yoga, Filament, and Jolt. Cross-browser validation is ongoing.
cards.label: See Valthorne in your browser

cards.title: Optional renderer limits
cards.text: The packaged desktop Filament path targets Windows x64. Compute-based desktop effects require OpenGL 4.3 and are unavailable on macOS OpenGL. Android is future work.
cards.label: Check backend support

pages.description: Ten focused examples, from an empty application to a playable FPS arena. Windows x64 packages include Java: extract a ZIP and open Start.bat.

pages.title: Your first frame starts here.
pages.description: Use Java 25, a desktop graphics driver with OpenGL 3.3 core, and your preferred Java build tool.

sections.title: 01 / Add Valthorne
sections.description: Native dependencies are included automatically. Use the complete integration guide for equivalent Kotlin and Maven configuration.

cards.title: Gradle, Kotlin, or Maven
cards.text: The complete guide includes both Gradle DSLs, Maven configuration, native access, and launch instructions.
cards.label: Open the integration guide

sections.title: 02 / Create an application
sections.description: Save this as src/main/java/game/Main.java. Allocate resources in init, advance the game in update, draw in render, and release owned resources in dispose.

cards.title: Run the application
cards.text: Use the Gradle wrapper from the repository. Run ./gradlew run, or ./gradlew.bat run in Windows PowerShell. Keep the documented native access and macOS flags.
cards.label: Full launch instructions

cards.title: Build your first scene
cards.text: Add a texture, a camera, and input. Keep resource ownership explicit and dispose graphics resources while the graphics context is alive.
cards.label: Understand the lifecycle

cards.title: Start from an example
cards.text: Explore the starter application or a focused graphics, physics, audio, or UI demo in the examples repository.
cards.label: Choose an example

pages.title: Built with the engine. Including this.
pages.description: This page is drawn by Valthorne's UI renderer. Start the animation to explore a Java-driven wireframe scene, then pause it to return to rendering only when something changes.

sections.title: A little world in Java
sections.description: A procedural UI drawing experiment: projected geometry and motion calculated in Java, painted through Valthorne Canvas2D. This is not a physics or 3D-renderer benchmark.

cards.title: A real Valthorne application
cards.text: JGL runs the application lifecycle. UIRoot manages the drawing context, a NanoContainer paints the site, and Canvas2D draws the layout, typography, and scene.
cards.label: View the website module

cards.title: A browser companion
cards.text: Native links, scrolling, keyboard focus, editable search, and copyable code remain available through HTML. Switch to Text version at any time for the full semantic document.
cards.label: Read the text version

cards.title: Idle means idle
cards.text: The host schedules a frame when content, input, images, or the viewport change. Only the opt-in animation requests continuous frames, and it pauses in hidden tabs.
cards.label: About the project
